title: Areas of climate stability of species ranges in the Brazilian Cerrado: disentangling uncertainties through time
problem: Identifying climatically stable areas for conservation is hampered by uncertainties from ecological and climate models, species' individual responses, and by common approaches that fail to simultaneously integrate species' past, present, and future distributions.
method: The paper proposes a hierarchical ANOVA on ensembles of ecological niche models for 18 tree species to partition uncertainties from models and time, thereby identifying climatically stable areas by comparing species' potential distributions across past, present, and future climate scenarios.
task: The task is to identify climatically stable areas for conservation in the Brazilian Cerrado by modeling tree species' distributions across past and future climates while statistically partitioning multiple sources of predictive uncertainty.

obs_and_metrics.observational_dataset: Nested ANOVA performed for each Cerrado cell
Nested ANOVA performed for each Cerrado cell

innovation: This paper introduces a hierarchical ANOVA-based method to partition uncertainties in ecological niche models and identify climatically stable areas in the Brazilian Cerrado by integrating species' range projections across past, present, and future time periods.

We downloaded climate variables from AOGCM outputs (monthly simulation for precipitation, and mean, maximum and minimum temperature), which were downscaled to the same grid and used to compute the full range of bioclimatic variables defined in the WorldClim database (see <http://www.worldclim.org/bioclim> and Additional Supporting Information for details). These AOGCMS were selected because for them there are compatible projections for past, current and future climate. We then selected five variables (annual mean temperature, temperature annual range, precipitation of wettest month, precipitation of driest month, and precipitation of warmest quarter) out of 19 bioclimatic variables using a factor analysis with Varimax rotation based on the correlation matrix among variables to minimize collinearity problems when building the ENMs.
